A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdvPrompter research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations, safety fine-tuning experiments, sampling ablations and PPO experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds HarmBench evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, cross-attack robustness tests and MT-bench measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the specified expansion from k candidates per beam to k/b candidates per beam, while both versions report k=48 and b=4. This is a limited revision to the stated search procedure; the alternating training framework, model architecture, replay buffer and gradient-free scoring remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds HarmBench's distinct harmful-behavior collection for attack and robustness evaluation, extending coverage beyond AdvBench. It also adds MT-bench conversational-utility evaluation after safety fine-tuning; AdvBench and MMLU remain.

E2.justification: Alongside retained GCG, AutoDAN and PPO comparisons, v2 evaluates PAIR, TAP, TAP-T and PAP-top5 in its HarmBench experiments. Appendix C.7.1 also compares BEAST against AdvPrompter on two Vicuna models. These are reported comparisons, not merely added citations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces training on HarmBench's 80 validation behaviors and testing on 320 test behaviors, its LLM evaluator, BEAST budgets of 10/60 seconds, and additional target configurations including Llama3.1-8b. The original AdvBench split and evaluators remain. The retained model-transfer comparison is labeled validation in v1 Figure 3 but test in v2 Table 5; this reported setting revision does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds source-model sensitivity analysis for transfer attacks (Table 9), tests whether safety fine-tuning transfers to GCG and AutoDAN on HarmBench (Table 8), and examines conversational utility. The original trial-count, decoding, amortized-AutoDAN and PPO analyses are retained, largely relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Three-independent-run averaging for the original AdvBench comparison is retained in v2 Table 3 and Figure 3, as are the existing shaded plots. No new seed-count, confidence-interval, significance-testing or uncertainty-reporting practice is specified.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial HarmBench, MT-bench, BEAST and source-model results. For example, Table 8 reports Mistral's GCG ASR falling from 63.4 to 57.8 and AutoDAN ASR from 71.0 to 35.0 after safety fine-tuning. Original whitebox and StrongREJECT numbers are retained. The Vicuna-7b, Llama2-7b and Mistral-7b transfer entries from v1 Figure 3 are omitted.

T1.justification: The formal q-step changes from minimizing L plus the AdvPrompter likelihood penalty in v1 Equation (6) to minimizing L in v2 Equation (5). Appendix B.2 retains the penalized derivation but explains bypassing that penalty through candidate sampling. The remaining mathematical framework is substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The core contribution remains fast, conditional adversarial generation through alternating training. v2 removes the approximately 800-fold headline speed claim and qualifies the introduction's performance-superiority claim. It also explicitly extends the claimed safety benefit from resistance to AdvPrompter to resistance against other attacks.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about AdvBench's semantic overlap and generalization evidence. It explains transfer performance through source-model difficulty and interprets weaker defense gains against GCG as a consequence of its high-perplexity attacks. These materially expand the paper's explanations and boundaries of defensive applicability.

D1.justification: v2 identifies HarmBench baseline implementations but shortens the warm-start recipe and omits v1's explicit greedy TargetLLM-generation disclosure. Core hyperparameters, hardware, PPO settings and code access remain. Its new 'around 10 hours' training-time statement conflicts with the retained 16-hour-12-minute and 20-hour-4-minute figures in Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: Mostly retained related-work text gains focused comparisons with LoFT, BEAST and AmpleGCG, plus references for TAP and HarmBench. These clarify distinctions involving proxy training, amortization and query budgets. Some broad application and amortized-optimization references are removed, without replacing the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and condenses the abstract, introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative. Related work, implementation details and most ablations move into reorganized appendices; experiments are framed explicitly around direct, data-transfer and model-transfer settings. An impact statement is added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main paper, adds multiple experimental tables, and redisplays selected original results in compact tables. The transfer bar chart is replaced by Table 5, the runtime chart gains baselines, and many retained figures and tables move to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v1's generalization evidence relied on AdvBench, and its defense evaluation principally used AdvPrompter itself. v2 adds HarmBench, broader baseline comparisons, cross-attack robustness tests and conversational-utility measurements, addressing important validation gaps. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses, including inconsistent training times and Table 11's claim of five targets despite displaying only two.
